## Summary
The event store and its delivery path as one concern (§12.5), backing the `EventWriter` seam P0.08 defined: batched ingest, `run_events` persistence with the visibility split and retention, fan-out, and the SSE route with exactly-once resumable replay. Implements ticket [`docs/tickets/09_P0.08b__run-events-and-streaming.md`](docs/tickets/09_P0.08b__run-events-and-streaming.md).

Stacked on `stevevitali/p0-08-run-orchestration` (PR #9).

## What changed
- **Storage** — `packages/db/migrations/0008_run_events.sql`: `run_events` daily RANGE partitions (`visibility=user`, project-lifetime) + a DEFAULT drop-nothing partition; `run_events_internal` (30-day retention, separate table, never streamed); `run_event_seq` per-run counter. `run_events`/`run_event_seq` FORCE-RLS; a `CHECK (visibility='user')` makes an internal-into-user mis-route impossible. Drizzle tables + parity/structural tests.
- **Writer** — `@rhema/orchestrator` `event-store.ts` `SqlEventWriter`: append inside the caller's tenant tx (REQ-DATA-33), gap-free `seq` via an atomic upsert, whitelist validation at the write boundary (REQ-DATA-37), the user/internal split, best-effort fan-out. `ensureRunEventsPartition` + `deleteExpiredInternalEvents`; `InMemoryRunEventBus`.
- **SSE** — `event-stream.ts` (`readUserEventsAfter`, `RunEventStreamer`, `streamRunEvents`, `formatSse`, density) + `apps/api/src/sse-routes.ts` `GET /runs/:id/events?after=<seq>`: replay-then-tail, reads only `run_events` (internal can't leak — REQ-ARCH-12), viewers get Summary / requester up to Verbose (REQ-DATA-38), `: ping` + no route buffering (REQ-ARCH-13), `?poll` finite replay for mobile (REQ-MOBILE-5).
- **Ingest** — `apps/run-task/src/event-buffer.ts` `EventBufferClient` + `FileBufferStore`: batch ≤250/2s, disk-buffer when the api is unreachable, land in order on recovery, pause past 5,000 buffered, drop nothing. The internal `POST events` endpoint rejects a >250 batch (413).
- **Maintenance** — `apps/worker/src/run-events-jobs.ts`: `run_events.retention` + `run_events.partition` handlers + queues.

## Design decisions
- One shared per-run `seq` space (gap-free) via a locked upsert; user rows → partitioned `run_events`, internal → `run_events_internal`. Seq gaps in the user stream (from internal events) are fine for `seq > after` replay.
- **Redis is a wakeup only, never a source of truth.** The tail always reads committed rows from Postgres; a lost/early/duplicate publish is at most a no-op; `Last-Event-ID` reconnect always replays exactly-once. Strict post-commit publish is the live Redis binding's job (deferred).
- `run_events_internal` is deliberately **not** under RLS (like `access_log`/`fetch_log`) so the system-scoped retention sweep works; it is never served, so the internal-leak guarantee is structural (the route reads only `run_events`).
- The SSE route scopes the run to the viewer's workspace **explicitly** (defense in depth alongside RLS, and the real gate under a superuser test connection).
